inputs.root_cause: 3 obligations (UBL-MODEL-001/PARSE-001/VALIDATE-001) shared an identical rule_text about the CBC XSD declaring elements typed via both qualified and unqualified data-type schemas. Previously declined for lacking clear spec grounding -- the referenced SAL facts were too generic. Event 195's exact_next_action flagged this cluster as worth re-checking against the pinned XSD directly, the same technique that unblocked 32 other UBL obligations this session.
inputs.acceptance_evidence: 5 new tests prove this package's typed-value system (Identifier/Amount/Quantity for udt:-restricted elements, Code for qdt:-restricted ones) correctly represents a concrete instance from each data-type schema family as genuinely distinct dataclasses.
inputs.regression_tier: full ubl package suite (tests/python/ubl) plus 6-format regression

execution_steps: 1. Extracted UBL-CommonBasicComponents-2.3.xsd from the pinned OASIS UBL 2.3 release ZIP and read its import declarations: it imports both qdt: (QualifiedDataTypes-2, UBL-QualifiedDataTypes-2.3.xsd) and udt: (bdndr:UnqualifiedDataTypes-1, BDNDR-UnqualifiedDataTypes-1.1.xsd) namespaces.

2. Read concrete complexType definitions directly: AccountIDType restricts udt:IdentifierType, PayableAmountType restricts udt:AmountType, InvoicedQuantityType restricts udt:QuantityType (all direct udt: restrictions) -- while PaymentMeansCodeType restricts qdt:PaymentMeansCodeType, itself restricting udt:CodeType (a qualification layer between the unqualified base and the cbc: element).

3. Counted restriction declarations across the whole file via regex: 1073 udt:-restricted elements vs 32 qdt:-restricted elements, confirming both categories are genuinely present and in active use, not a marginal or theoretical distinction.

4. Deliberately did NOT write a test that re-parses the XSD at runtime: the acquired schema lives under the gitignored .local/format-contracts/acquired/ cache, not guaranteed present in every checkout, so a runtime dependency on it would make the test non-portable, unlike every other test in this suite. Instead wrote tests proving the underlying fact the rule_text protects -- that the runtime type system genuinely distinguishes udt:-restricted (Identifier/Amount/Quantity) from qdt:-restricted (Code) elements as distinct dataclasses.

5. Ran ruff (clean) and the full ubl suite (776 passed, was 771, +5) before writing any evidence claim. Ran the full 6-format regression (3039 passed, was 3034, +5; same 4 pre-existing unrelated safetensors interop failures, 2 skipped) confirming zero cross-format regression.
tests_run: .venv/Scripts/pytest tests/python/ipynb tests/python/ora tests/python/nrrd tests/python/xliff tests/python/safetensors tests/python/ubl -q -- 3039 passed, 2 skipped, 4 preexisting unrelated safetensors interop failures, was 3034 passed

evidence.oracle: Verified against the pinned OASIS UBL 2.3 release package's own vendored XSD schema (extracted directly from the ZIP, not a SAL-fact paraphrase or memory) -- higher-confidence than typical SELF-CONSISTENT evidence, though still not cross-checked against an independent reference UBL implementation, per GAP-008. The test artifact itself deliberately does not depend on the gitignored XSD cache at runtime, for portability.
evidence.obligations_moved_breakdown: 3 obligations closed by proving the qualified/unqualified data-type schema distinction the rule_text describes is genuinely reflected in the runtime type system, grounded in a direct read of the pinned authoritative XSD rather than the previously-insufficient generic SAL facts.
